reader: Claude third reader (assigned by the Claude coordinator)
method: Original paper and scheme renders in original-pages/ read for every item. Rules: PLAN R7/R9, CARD-STANDARD sections 5 and 9, standard-model/stage1/READING.md rule 6 for printed choices. Splitting rule applied across all LCVP packets: a separately printed instruction (its own sentence), or an item the paper itself names, that the scheme marks separately is its own card; a single compound instruction ('identify and explain', 'identify and describe', 'state and explain') whose (1+1) or (2+2) sits inside each answer point stays one card. Filing: evaluating or planning a specific activity goes with that activity's unit, as the live 2015-2026 filings do.

splitValidation.reason: Paper p13 Q3(i) demands one positive and one negative effect of moving to selling online, two things the paper itself names, and scheme p8 prints a separate pool for each (seven positive, six negative) at 2 x 2 marks (1+1), so the student answers two things separately for separate marks (R7); the informed 2+2 is confirmed.

splitDifferences.reason: Paper p13 Q3(ii) is one compound instruction, 'Identify and explain three issues', and scheme p8 pays 3 x 2 marks (1+1) per issue with each model printing the issue and its explanation together, so the (1+1) is the inside of each answer point, not two separately answered asks; the issues (market research, finance, staff, production, premises, legalities) are planning a business, filed as 2011 B3(ii) is.

Paper p25 Q3(c) is one compound instruction, 'Identify and describe two skills', and scheme p13 pays 2 x 4 marks (2+2) per skill while printing only skill names, so it is two answer points of 4 marks on one card, with the scoped no-answer notice for the unprinted descriptions.

perCardSubject: outline how each source was relevant

splitDifferences.reason: Paper p34 Q6(c) prints two separate instructions, 'State four sources of information used...' and 'Outline how each source was relevant', and scheme p16-17 pays 4 x 2 marks (1+1) with each model printed as source then relevance, so each printed ask has its own 4 marks (R7, the CARD-STANDARD 'prints two asks' case); the two models without a relevance line need the scoped no-answer notice on the relevance card.

Paper p37 Q7(c) is one compound instruction, 'Identify and explain four forms of promotion', and scheme p18 pays 4 x 2 marks (1+1) per form while printing only the forms, so it stays one 8-mark card with the scoped no-answer notice for the explanations.

filingDifferences.reason: Paper p11 Q1 is one printed 'explain three of the following terms' choice (overheads, diversification, innovation, mentor) marked alike at 3 x 2 (1+1) on scheme p7; under READING rule 6 the two headings covering most of it are Local Business Enterprises (overheads, diversification) and Enterprise Skills (innovation, mentor), flagged CHOICE SPANS.

Paper p13 asks a positive effect for an enterprise moving to selling online and scheme p8 pays business-operation effects (trading hours, lower rent, more stock, bigger customer base, discount codes, reviews), which is how a business operates, not a personal enterprise skill.

Paper p13 asks a negative effect of selling online and scheme p8 pays business-operation costs and risks (returns, packaging and delivery, website, payment security, lost offline customers), filed with its positive twin.

Paper p20 asks why employers emphasise communication skills when hiring and scheme p10 pays 3 x 3 (1+1+1) for what the workplace needs (contact with others, teamwork, customers, instructions, conflict), filed as the live 2020 Q1(c) 'why this employer wants excellent communication skills' card is.

Paper p22 Q2(c)(i), in a question on community associations, asks steps to prepare the visit of a voluntary organisation's representative and scheme p11 pays 2 x 1 for arranging that visit; a visit-in from a voluntary body is filed as the live 2016 Q5 visit-in asks are.

Paper p23 asks ways to evaluate the success of that voluntary-organisation visit and scheme p12 pays 3 x 3 (1+1+1) for methods aimed at it (questionnaire to the speaker, contacting the speaker, reviewing the visit's aims); evaluating a visit goes with the visit, as live 2023 Q6(d) and 2024 Q2(d) are.

Paper p24 asks the agenda for the class meeting to organise the end-of-year awards ceremony and scheme p12 pays 4 x 1 for planning items for that class activity (officers, tasks, finance, plan of work, timeline), filed as the 2010 Q5(a) and live 2025 Q5(a) class-activity agendas are.

Paper p27 Q4(a) asks four sources of employment in the local area and scheme p14 pays 4 x 1 for any workplaces named, i.e. local employers; live 2018 Q3(a), the same ask, is under Local Business Enterprises, and the model lane's pass C moved the 2022 June local-economy part out of Work Placement for the same reason.

Paper p30 asks why it is important for a business to plan and scheme p15 pays 3 x 2 (1+1) for business reasons (viability, loans and grants, measuring progress, decisions, efficiency), filed as the live 2023 Q4(a) 'why plan for the future' business card is.

Paper p31 asks how Francis could evaluate his enterprise's success and scheme p15 pays 4 x 2 (1+1) for business measures (profit, market share, awards, staff relations, customer loyalty, expansion, continuity), filed as the live 2023 Q4(d) business-evaluation card is.

Paper p35 asks whether the LCVP prepares students with the skills to succeed in the modern world of work and scheme p17 pays 3 x 3 (1+1+1), YES or NO; the live 2019 Q4(d) card with the same wording is under Introduction to Working Life.

Paper p38 asks how taking part in organising and running the class swap-shop social enterprise benefits the student and scheme p18 pays 3 x 3 (1+1+1) for what the activity teaches; benefits of the class enterprise activity are filed under An Enterprise Activity as live 2016 Q2(c) and 2026 Q7(c) are.
